titre: 6 Things a High-Status Woman Never Does in Conversation #elegance #highvaluewoman #etiquette #smartgirl #selfimprovement
notes: Schéma high-status-woman (f6b8b58a r 5,51 sur 7 passages ; 4950b76f r 8,87 ; 2f3248a3 r 5,35 ; 40829b2f r 3,43). Accroches écrites : « 6 Things a High-Status Woman Never Does in Conversation » (retenue : le gagnant « 7 Things a High-Status Woman Never Does » avec un twist, la conversation, qui garde l'élégance du côté de la culture et des manières), « Timeless things every woman should learn » (écartée : la version « own » portait sur des bijoux), « Small habits that make a woman look highly educated » (écartée : plus loin du gabarit). Title Case comme @richgirlacadmy_1, sans émojis (ils ne passent pas au rendu). Six items de manières, neufs face aux deux inspirations : ne pas faire semblant d'avoir lu un livre, ne pas corriger en public, ne pas ramener l'histoire à soi, présenter les gens, préférer le mot clair au mot savant, ne pas dire « je suis nulle en histoire ». Aucun conseil d'argent ni de marque. Sophia sur le dernier item, en « she », avec la formule « a micro-learning app like the Sophia app ». Images de la banque du label, sans texte ni marque (1a404ee4, bab96c09, 084843d8 écartées) ; slide Sophia sur un tableau et des bougies, sans personne.

slides.texte_overlay:
6 Things a High-Status
Woman Never Does
in Conversation

1. She Never Pretends to Have
Read the Book.
She says "I haven't read it
yet. What is it about?"
Admitting what you don't know
is quiet confidence.

2. She Never Corrects
Someone in Front of Others.
A wrong date, a mispronounced
name. If it matters, she says
it later, in private.

3. She Never Turns Your Story
Into Her Own.
No "that happened to me too."
She stays on your story and
asks what happened next.

4. She Never Forgets
to Introduce People.
When two friends meet through
her, she gives each a name and
one thing they have in common.

5. She Never Uses Big Words
to Impress.
She picks the clearest word.
Real eloquence is being
understood the first time.

6. She Never Says "I'm Bad
at History."
She says "I haven't learned
it yet," then learns a little
every day. Art, history,
science, 5 minutes at a time.
